You are a hostile, independent reviewer with fresh context. Read-only: you MUST NOT edit, create, or commit anything, and must not run state-changing git commands.

START YOUR FINAL ANSWER WITH ONE WORD: ALLOW or BLOCK.

WHAT TO REVIEW: branch night/2026-08-18-plainer-bp in /private/tmp/live-spec-night18/wt-a2-bp, against its base (the branch point on night/2026-08-18-integration — find it with `git merge-base night/2026-08-18-integration HEAD`). Four commits touching skills/build-pipeline/SKILL.md, guardrails/rule-census.json and README.md.

THE CLAIM: 101 over-length sentences and 110 style findings were repaired by REWRITING — each long sentence split into two or three short ones with every term, number, requirement and spec code preserved; each style finding repaired by stating the claim positively rather than by deleting information. Findings fell 211 → 37. The file GREW (53,492 → 55,475 bytes), which is expected: splitting costs words. This lane is about readability, not weight.

YOUR JOB: pick FIFTEEN rewritten passages AT RANDOM across the whole diff — not the first fifteen, not the easy ones; spread them over different sections, and include at least three of the longest original sentences and at least three style repairs. For each, put the old and new text side by side and judge against the pack's own discipline in skills/text-audit/references/rewrite-meaning-check.md (read it first). For every one of the fifteen, answer explicitly:

- ACTOR: is the same party doing the thing? (A rewrite that turns "the worker halts" into "work halts" has lost the actor.)
- FORCE: is the same obligation carried? ("must" → "should", "never" → "avoid", an imperative → a description = a loss.)
- CONDITION: same trigger, same "when"?
- SCOPE: same breadth — every tree, every push, all three cases?
- THRESHOLD: every number, limit and unit still present and unchanged?
- EXCEPTION: did a carve-out silently vanish? This is the commonest real loss when a "X, not Y" frame is repaired — Y sometimes carried a genuine exclusion.
- OUTPUT and SIDE EFFECT: same artifact produced, same consequence stated?

Then check these mechanically over the whole diff, not just your fifteen:
1. Did any spec code, path, backticked literal, [tag], "base rule N" or numeric threshold disappear? Compare multisets of those tokens between the old and new file (use `git show <base>:skills/build-pipeline/SKILL.md`). Report anything lost OR anything newly invented.
2. Was any test edited to match new prose? Diff tests/ — the claim is that no test changed. Verify.
3. Are the phrases that tests pin still present VERBATIM, in the same case? Take the pinned needles from the tests that read this file and grep the new SKILL.md for each.
4. The three structural moves claimed to add and remove nothing (a numbered list, five tripwire lines, two rosters taking a colon) — verify each really moved no content.
5. One deliberate wording change is admitted: "So the pipeline is not trusted, it is ENFORCED" → "So the pipeline is enforced by a machine." Judge it: did the negated half carry a requirement the reader needs?
6. guardrails/rule-census.json: verify the recorded ceilings only FELL. A raised ceiling anywhere is a BLOCK.

BLOCK on substance: a lost requirement, a softened obligation, a vanished exception, a dropped number, an edited test, a raised ceiling, or a rewrite that reads well but says less. Do not BLOCK on taste — if a sentence is merely plainer than you would have written it, that is the point of the lane.

If you BLOCK, name the single strongest loss first, quoting old and new text with line numbers, and say what would turn it into ALLOW. If you ALLOW, list every place where the meaning shifted even slightly, and say why each is acceptable.

Do not take the worker's report on trust — you have not been shown it, for that reason. Verify in the tree.

reds, so a new file is measured and recorded before it can pass.

`evals/fixtures/text-audit/` holds three short texts, each carrying one known defect. The test

rewrite. A worker that misses the changed actor, the softened force, or the dropped exception has

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""check-doc-findings-bound.py — gate aa: no live document carries more findings than its record.

THE LAW (the owner's word, 2026-07-28 evening): a document repaired to zero stays at zero, on every
push, with no exception. A document still carrying findings never carries more than it did. The
direction of the count is down and never up.

WHAT IT READS. `guardrails/rule-census.json` holds one entry per live document with the count recorded
when it was last measured. `scripts/rule-census.py` measures the live set the same way for both, so the
record and the measure can never drift apart in method.

THE THREE VERDICTS.

  (a) measured == recorded, and recorded is 0  -> pass, and the document is named as held clean.
  (b) measured  < recorded                     -> pass, and the gate prints the re-seed command, so the
      lower number becomes the new ceiling rather than leaving headroom the next edit can spend.
  (c) measured  > recorded                     -> RED. A document recorded at 0 reds on its first
      finding, which is the uncompromising half of the law.

A live document missing from the record also reds: a new document is measured and recorded before it
can pass, so nothing enters the tree unmeasured.

WHY IT SITS AT THE PUSH. The census is a report and reports do not refuse anything. Between the morning
of 2026-07-28 and that evening one page rose from 107 findings to 112 with nothing noticing. This gate
is what noticing looks like.

THE SECOND ARM: THE RECORD ITSELF (SPEC INV-301, R302.11 to R302.15). The verdicts above hold the law
over the DOCUMENTS. The record is a file a person can edit, so this arm holds the law over the RECORD.
It reads the record against the copy the base commit holds and reds an entry whose recorded count rose
with no reason beside it. A raise is lawful when the entry carries a non-empty `reason` field, which is the
shape `guardrails/doc-bounds.json` already uses for a raised byte ceiling; inventing a second shape for
one idea is what the pack's one-home rule forbids. The writing arm lives in `scripts/rule-census.py`,
which refuses to store a rise at all, so between the two of them the printed remedy can only lower a
number.

WHY THIS ARM SITS HERE AND NOT UNDER A GATE LETTER OF ITS OWN. One law takes one gate letter. Gate aa
already owns "a recorded count moves down alone", and the record is the other half of that one law, so a
new letter would owe an entry in `guardrails/gate-red-proofs.json` for a fact this gate already stands
for. The arm's own red proof rides gate aa's registered entry.

WHICH COPY IT READS AGAINST, AND WHY NOT `HEAD`. This gate runs from `guardrails/pre-push` and from the
CI mirror, and at both of those moments the raise is ALREADY COMMITTED. An arm comparing the working
folder against `HEAD` therefore reads two copies that agree, prints nothing, and passes every real push;
it reaches an uncommitted edit alone, and a push never carries one. The honest ground for a gate on the
push chain is the state the REMOTE ALREADY HOLDS, so the arm reads the record against a BASE COMMIT.

HOW THE BASE COMMIT IS RESOLVED. Through the same ladder `guardrails/check-prover-record.sh` reads, so
one idea keeps one shape: the environment value `LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE` where it resolves to a commit (CI
passes the push event's base commit, a planted test passes its own), then `origin/main`, then the commit
before the tip. A fourth rung follows the first three: the TIP ITSELF, which is the only copy a
repository holding one commit and no upstream can reach, and which keeps the arm's reach over an
uncommitted hand edit in such a tree. Each run names the rung it read, so the arm's ground is visible.

HOW IT READS THAT COPY. It asks git, through `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` beside the record and then
`git show <base>:<path>`. Where git answers nothing — no repository, no commit yet, no copy of that
record at the base, or a copy that will not parse — the arm STANDS DOWN BY NAME and says what it read
nothing of (INV-218's shape). That covers a fresh clone, a machine with no network, and the first push
of a branch whose base holds no record; none of them is evidence of a raise, and the document arm above
still holds. The CI mirror answers the same question the same way: `.github/workflows/gates.yml` hands
gate aa the event's base commit in `LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE`, and a pull request with no such value falls to
`origin/main`, which the full-depth checkout carries.

WHY AN UNCHANGED RECORD IS SILENT. The arm speaks only of an entry whose recorded count ROSE against the
base copy. A record identical to that copy yields no such entry, so the arm prints nothing and the
gate's verdict is the document arm's alone. A gate that reds on an unchanged tree blocks every push in
the repository, which is the failure this silence avoids.

Usage:
  check-doc-findings-bound.py                    push mode: the repository's own record and live set.
  check-doc-findings-bound.py --record FILE      read the record from FILE (fixtures).
  check-doc-findings-bound.py --root DIR         measure the live set under DIR (fixtures).
Exit 0 when every document sits at or under its record and no recorded count rose by hand with no
reason; exit 1 naming each document that rose and each record entry raised without one.
Stdlib only.
"""
import argparse
import importlib.util
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

SCRIPT_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(SCRIPT_DIR)
CENSUS = os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "scripts", "rule-census.py")
RECORD = os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "guardrails", "rule-census.json")

CHECK = "doc-findings-bound"
# The base the record is read against, named the way `guardrails/check-prover-record.sh` names it.
BASE_ENV = "LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE"
EMPTY_SHA = "0" * 40


def load_census():
    """The census module itself, so the gate and the report measure by one definition."""
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("rule_census", CENSUS)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def base_commit(top):
    """The commit the record is read against, by the ladder the prover-record gate already reads.

    `LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE` where it resolves, then `origin/main`, then the commit before the tip, then
    the tip itself. Returns the ref name, or None where the repository holds no commit at all.
    """
    ladder = []
    stated = (os.environ.get(BASE_ENV) or "").strip()
    if stated and stated != EMPTY_SHA:
        ladder.append(stated)
    ladder += ["origin/main", "HEAD~1", "HEAD"]
    for ref in ladder:
        proc = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", top, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet",
                               "%s^{commit}" % ref], capture_output=True, text=True)
        if proc.returncode == 0 and proc.stdout.strip():
            return ref
    return None


def base_record(path):
    """The record's `files` as the base commit holds it, or a note saying what git answered nothing of.

    Returns (files, ref, None) on success and (None, ref, note) where no base copy can be read.
    """
    # The real path on both sides: git answers with symlinks resolved, and a temporary directory under
    # /var on this platform is reached through one, which would otherwise make the two paths disagree.
    real = os.path.realpath(path)
    directory = os.path.dirname(real) or "."
    try:
        top = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", directory, "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"],
                             capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    except OSError as e:
        return None, None, "no git command answered here (%s)" % e
    if not top:
        return None, None, "no git repository holds %s" % path
    ref = base_commit(top)
    if not ref:
        return None, None, "no commit in %s holds a record to read against" % top
    rel = os.path.relpath(real, os.path.realpath(top))
    proc = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", top, "show", "%s:%s" % (ref, rel)],
                          capture_output=True, text=True)
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        return None, ref, "%s holds no copy of %s" % (ref, rel)
    try:
        return json.loads(proc.stdout)["files"], ref, None
    except (ValueError, KeyError) as e:
        return None, ref, "the copy of %s at %s would not be read (%s)" % (rel, ref, e)


def hand_raises(recorded, base):
    """Every entry whose recorded count rose against the base copy while carrying no reason."""
    out = []
    for rel, entry in sorted(recorded.items()):
        was = base.get(rel)
        if not isinstance(was, dict) or not isinstance(entry, dict):
            continue
        if entry.get("total", 0) <= was.get("total", 0):
            continue
        if str(entry.get("reason") or "").strip():
            continue
        out.append((rel, was.get("total", 0), entry.get("total", 0)))
    return out


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--record", default=RECORD)
    ap.add_argument("--root", default=REPO_ROOT)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    try:
        with open(args.record, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            recorded = json.load(f)["files"]
    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError) as e:
        print("FAIL (%s): cannot read the record %s (%s) — the record is this gate's whole ground, "
              "and a gate with no ground passes on everything." % (CHECK, args.record, e))
        return 1

    base, base_ref, stood_down = base_record(args.record)
    raised = hand_raises(recorded, base) if base is not None else []

    census = load_census()
    cap, cap_rule = census.load_word_cap()
    files = census.live_files(args.root)
    if not files:
        print("FAIL (%s): the live set came out empty, so this gate would pass on nothing." % CHECK)
        return 1

    rose, fell, held, unrecorded = [], [], [], []
    for rel in files:
        reading = census.measure(rel, cap, root=args.root)
        if "unread" in reading:
            print("FAIL (%s): %s refused to be read (%s)." % (CHECK, rel, reading["unread"]))
            return 1
        total = reading["total"]
        if rel not in recorded:
            unrecorded.append((rel, total))
            continue
        bound = recorded[rel]["total"]
        if total > bound:
            rose.append((rel, bound, total, reading))
        elif total < bound:
            fell.append((rel, bound, total))
        elif bound == 0:
            held.append(rel)

    for rel in held:
        print("  held clean: %s" % rel)
    for rel, bound, total in fell:
        print("  fell: %s — recorded %d, measured %d" % (rel, bound, total))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""check-doc-findings-bound.py — gate aa: no live document carries more findings than its record.

THE LAW (the owner's word, 2026-07-28 evening): a document repaired to zero stays at zero, on every
push, with no exception. A document still carrying findings never carries more than it did. The
direction of the count is down and never up.

WHAT IT READS. `guardrails/rule-census.json` holds one entry per live document with the count recorded
when it was last measured. `scripts/rule-census.py` measures the live set the same way for both, so the
record and the measure can never drift apart in method.

THE THREE VERDICTS.

  (a) measured == recorded, and recorded is 0  -> pass, and the document is named as held clean.
  (b) measured  < recorded                     -> pass, and the gate prints the re-seed command, so the
      lower number becomes the new ceiling rather than leaving headroom the next edit can spend.
  (c) measured  > recorded                     -> RED. A document recorded at 0 reds on its first
      finding, which is the uncompromising half of the law.

A live document missing from the record also reds: a new document is measured and recorded before it
can pass, so nothing enters the tree unmeasured.

WHY IT SITS AT THE PUSH. The census is a report and reports do not refuse anything. Between the morning
of 2026-07-28 and that evening one page rose from 107 findings to 112 with nothing noticing. This gate
is what noticing looks like.

THE SECOND ARM: THE RECORD ITSELF (SPEC INV-301, R302.11 to R302.15). The verdicts above hold the law
over the DOCUMENTS. The record is a file a person can edit, so this arm holds the law over the RECORD.
It reads the record against the copy the base commit holds and reds an entry whose recorded count rose
with no reason beside it. A raise is lawful when the entry carries a non-empty `reason` field, which is the
shape `guardrails/doc-bounds.json` already uses for a raised byte ceiling; inventing a second shape for
one idea is what the pack's one-home rule forbids. The writing arm lives in `scripts/rule-census.py`,
which refuses to store a rise at all, so between the two of them the printed remedy can only lower a
number.

WHY THIS ARM SITS HERE AND NOT UNDER A GATE LETTER OF ITS OWN. One law takes one gate letter. Gate aa
already owns "a recorded count moves down alone", and the record is the other half of that one law, so a
new letter would owe an entry in `guardrails/gate-red-proofs.json` for a fact this gate already stands
for. The arm's own red proof rides gate aa's registered entry.

WHICH COPY IT READS AGAINST, AND WHY NOT `HEAD`. This gate runs from `guardrails/pre-push` and from the
CI mirror, and at both of those moments the raise is ALREADY COMMITTED. An arm comparing the working
folder against `HEAD` therefore reads two copies that agree, prints nothing, and passes every real push;
it reaches an uncommitted edit alone, and a push never carries one. The honest ground for a gate on the
push chain is the state the REMOTE ALREADY HOLDS, so the arm reads the record against a BASE COMMIT.

HOW THE BASE COMMIT IS RESOLVED. Through the same ladder `guardrails/check-prover-record.sh` reads, so
one idea keeps one shape: the environment value `LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE` where it resolves to a commit (CI
passes the push event's base commit, a planted test passes its own), then `origin/main`, then the commit
before the tip. A fourth rung follows the first three: the TIP ITSELF, which is the only copy a
repository holding one commit and no upstream can reach, and which keeps the arm's reach over an
uncommitted hand edit in such a tree. Each run names the rung it read, so the arm's ground is visible.

HOW IT READS THAT COPY. It asks git, through `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` beside the record and then
`git show <base>:<path>`. Where git answers nothing — no repository, no commit yet, no copy of that
record at the base, or a copy that will not parse — the arm STANDS DOWN BY NAME and says what it read
nothing of (INV-218's shape). That covers a fresh clone, a machine with no network, and the first push
of a branch whose base holds no record; none of them is evidence of a raise, and the document arm above
still holds. The CI mirror answers the same question the same way: `.github/workflows/gates.yml` hands
gate aa the event's base commit in `LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE`, and a pull request with no such value falls to
`origin/main`, which the full-depth checkout carries.

WHY AN UNCHANGED RECORD IS SILENT. The arm speaks only of an entry whose recorded count ROSE against the
base copy. A record identical to that copy yields no such entry, so the arm prints nothing and the
gate's verdict is the document arm's alone. A gate that reds on an unchanged tree blocks every push in
the repository, which is the failure this silence avoids.

Usage:
  check-doc-findings-bound.py                    push mode: the repository's own record and live set.
  check-doc-findings-bound.py --record FILE      read the record from FILE (fixtures).
  check-doc-findings-bound.py --root DIR         measure the live set under DIR (fixtures).
Exit 0 when every document sits at or under its record and no recorded count rose by hand with no
reason; exit 1 naming each document that rose and each record entry raised without one.
Stdlib only.
"""
import argparse
import importlib.util
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

SCRIPT_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(SCRIPT_DIR)
CENSUS = os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "scripts", "rule-census.py")
RECORD = os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "guardrails", "rule-census.json")

CHECK = "doc-findings-bound"
# The base the record is read against, named the way `guardrails/check-prover-record.sh` names it.
BASE_ENV = "LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE"
EMPTY_SHA = "0" * 40


def load_census():
    """The census module itself, so the gate and the report measure by one definition."""
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("rule_census", CENSUS)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def base_commit(top):
    """The commit the record is read against, by the ladder the prover-record gate already reads.

    `LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE` where it resolves, then `origin/main`, then the commit before the tip, then
    the tip itself. Returns the ref name, or None where the repository holds no commit at all.
    """
    ladder = []
    stated = (os.environ.get(BASE_ENV) or "").strip()
    if stated and stated != EMPTY_SHA:
        ladder.append(stated)
    ladder += ["origin/main", "HEAD~1", "HEAD"]
    for ref in ladder:
        proc = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", top, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet",
                               "%s^{commit}" % ref], capture_output=True, text=True)
        if proc.returncode == 0 and proc.stdout.strip():
            return ref
    return None


def base_record(path):
    """The record's `files` as the base commit holds it, or a note saying what git answered nothing of.

    Returns (files, ref, None) on success and (None, ref, note) where no base copy can be read.
    """
    # The real path on both sides: git answers with symlinks resolved, and a temporary directory under
    # /var on this platform is reached through one, which would otherwise make the two paths disagree.
    real = os.path.realpath(path)
    directory = os.path.dirname(real) or "."
    try:
        top = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", directory, "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"],
                             capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    except OSError as e:
        return None, None, "no git command answered here (%s)" % e
    if not top:
        return None, None, "no git repository holds %s" % path
    ref = base_commit(top)
    if not ref:
        return None, None, "no commit in %s holds a record to read against" % top
    rel = os.path.relpath(real, os.path.realpath(top))
    proc = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", top, "show", "%s:%s" % (ref, rel)],
                          capture_output=True, text=True)
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        return None, ref, "%s holds no copy of %s" % (ref, rel)
    try:
        return json.loads(proc.stdout)["files"], ref, None
    except (ValueError, KeyError) as e:
        return None, ref, "the copy of %s at %s would not be read (%s)" % (rel, ref, e)


def hand_raises(recorded, base):
    """Every entry whose recorded count rose against the base copy while carrying no reason."""
    out = []
    for rel, entry in sorted(recorded.items()):
        was = base.get(rel)
        if not isinstance(was, dict) or not isinstance(entry, dict):
            continue
        if entry.get("total", 0) <= was.get("total", 0):
            continue
        if str(entry.get("reason") or "").strip():
            continue
        out.append((rel, was.get("total", 0), entry.get("total", 0)))
    return out


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--record", default=RECORD)
    ap.add_argument("--root", default=REPO_ROOT)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    try:
        with open(args.record, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            recorded = json.load(f)["files"]
    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError) as e:
        print("FAIL (%s): cannot read the record %s (%s) — the record is this gate's whole ground, "
              "and a gate with no ground passes on everything." % (CHECK, args.record, e))
        return 1

    base, base_ref, stood_down = base_record(args.record)
    raised = hand_raises(recorded, base) if base is not None else []

    census = load_census()
    cap, cap_rule = census.load_word_cap()
    files = census.live_files(args.root)
    if not files:
        print("FAIL (%s): the live set came out empty, so this gate would pass on nothing." % CHECK)
        return 1

    rose, fell, held, unrecorded = [], [], [], []
    for rel in files:
        reading = census.measure(rel, cap, root=args.root)
        if "unread" in reading:
            print("FAIL (%s): %s refused to be read (%s)." % (CHECK, rel, reading["unread"]))
            return 1
        total = reading["total"]
        if rel not in recorded:
            unrecorded.append((rel, total))
            continue
        bound = recorded[rel]["total"]
        if total > bound:
            rose.append((rel, bound, total, reading))
        elif total < bound:
            fell.append((rel, bound, total))
        elif bound == 0:
            held.append(rel)

    for rel in held:
        print("  held clean: %s" % rel)
    for rel, bound, total in fell:
        print("  fell: %s — recorded %d, measured %d" % (rel, bound, total))
    if fell:
        print("  Lower the ceiling to what the text now measures:")
        print("    python3 scripts/rule-census.py --json guardrails/rule-census.json")

    if stood_down:
        print("  stands down: the record arm read no base copy of the record — %s." % stood_down)
    else:
        print("  the record arm read the record against the copy %s holds." % base_ref)

    if not rose and not unrecorded and not raised:
        print("OK (%s): %d live documents, %d held at zero, none above its record (cap %d, rule %s)."
              % (CHECK, len(files), len(held), cap, cap_rule))
        return 0

    for rel, was, now in raised:
        print("FAIL (%s): the record for %s was raised from %d to %d against the copy %s holds, with no "
              "reason beside it. A raise states its reason in that entry's `reason` field, the way a "
              "raised byte ceiling does in guardrails/doc-bounds.json."
              % (CHECK, rel, was, now, base_ref))
    for rel, total in unrecorded:
        print("FAIL (%s): %s is live and carries no entry in the record. Measure it into the record "
              "before it ships: python3 scripts/rule-census.py --json guardrails/rule-census.json"
              % (CHECK, rel))
    for rel, bound, total, reading in rose:
        if bound == 0:
            print("FAIL (%s): %s was repaired to zero and now carries %d finding(s). A cleared document "
                  "stays cleared." % (CHECK, rel, total))
        else:
            print("FAIL (%s): %s rose from %d to %d findings." % (CHECK, rel, bound, total))
        print("    long %d (longest sentence %d words), style %d, register %d"
              % (reading["long"], reading["longest"], reading["style"], reading["register"]))
    if rose:
        print("  Fix: repair the text, or read `python3 scripts/rule-census.py %s` to see each "
              "finding." % rose[0][0])
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

ALLOW

## What I verified (in the tree, not from any report)

**Scope of change** — `git diff 25acaf5b3335..HEAD --name-only` returns exactly three files: `README.md`, `guardrails/rule-census.json`, `skills/build-pipeline/SKILL.md`. Base = `git merge-base night/2026-08-18-integration HEAD` = `25acaf5`.

**Mechanical checks over the whole diff**

1. **Token multisets** (whitespace-normalized, so line-rewraps don't create false hits) between `git show 25acaf5:skills/build-pipeline/SKILL.md` and the new file:
   - backticked literals — **LOST {} / NEW {}**
   - `[tag]` brackets — **LOST {} / NEW {}**
   - spec codes (`SPEC INV-n`, `T-n`, `E-n`, `M-n`) — **LOST {} / NEW {}**
   - `base rule N` and `rule N` — **LOST {} / NEW {}**
   - all numerals/thresholds — **LOST {} / NEW {}** (≥ 1 row, ~30 days, three rounds, 0.x.0, 2026-07-15, INV numbers all intact)
   - paths — only trailing-period artifacts (`github.com/happysasha18/live-spec.`, `design-sync/snapshot.`); no path lost or invented.
2. **No test edited.** `git diff --name-only` shows nothing under `tests/`, `evals/`, `scripts/`, `guardrails/*.py`, `.github/`. The only `guardrails/` change is the census JSON.
3. **Pinned needles present verbatim.** I ran all 35 test files that read `skills/build-pipeline/SKILL.md`: **548 passed, 14 skipped, 1 failed** — the one failure is `test_worker_restore.py::test_the_gate_runs_against_this_machines_own_transcripts`, which reads *live agent transcripts on this machine* and reds on another session's `git checkout --` (transcript path `…/61f5a05d-…/agent-aa555a235fb6a9f92.jsonl`). Environmental, not this diff. A separate whole-suite pass also hit `test_config_health` for four installed skills drifting from source (`build-pipeline`, `communicator`, `live-spec-base`, `publish`) — three of those four are untouched by this branch, so it is a worktree/`~/.claude` artifact, not a regression.
4. **Structural moves add and remove nothing** — verified by extraction, not by eye:
   - Request-kind roster: old parenthetical vs new "The kinds are:" — the two strings are **byte-identical** across all eleven members.
   - Step roster: `1 spec · 2 prove · … · 9 commit & show · design-sync/snapshot` — **byte-identical** old vs new.
   - Five tripwire lines: the run-on `·` chain became five bullets; all five predicates survive, and the trailing force `Any one of them makes the wish ⇒ FEATURE, however casually asked` restores the disjunction the bullets would otherwise have lost.
   - Numbered list: the four class-hunt moves (198-word sentence) became `1.`–`4.`; every clause including `(base rule 14)`, `ARCHITECTURE.md in the same change`, `fixed first so the prover can flag it`, and `does not guess it` survives.
5. **Census ceilings only fell.** Programmatic compare of every entry's `total`/`long`/`style`/`register`: no key added or removed, and **no field rose anywhere**. Three totals fell: `README.md` 13→4, `docs/adoption.md` 6→5, `skills/build-pipeline/SKILL.md` 211→37. `OVERVIEW.md`'s `longest` 67→98 is *not* an enforced field — `guardrails/check-doc-findings-bound.py` gates on `total` only, and `hand_raises()` reads `total`. I ran the gate: `OK (doc-findings-bound): 146 live documents, 26 held at zero, none above its record`, with **no `fell:` lines**, i.e. the record now matches a fresh measure exactly. `spec-style-lint` independently reports `errors 1, warnings 32` = the recorded `style: 33`.
6. **README's generated block is true**: `cat skills/*/SKILL.md skills/*/references/*.md | wc -l` = 5907 and `cat skills/*/SKILL.md | wc -l` = 3752, matching the two numbers written.

## The fifteen passages, judged against `rewrite-meaning-check.md`

Three longest originals first (198w / 81w / 81w / 78w / 77w by the census's own `prose_sentences` splitter).

**1. The class hunt — the 198-word sentence (bug door).** Old `(1) name the defect abstractly … (2) check the architecture … (3) check the spec … (4) escalate to the human …` → four numbered items. ACTOR: same throughout (the reader; "the method stops and asks"). FORCE: `fix all siblings in the same change`, `updates ARCHITECTURE.md in the same change`, `fixed first`, `does not guess it` all carried; nothing became "should". CONDITION: `A confirmed bug drives a class hunt before it closes (SPEC INV-124)` unchanged. SCOPE: `every surface where that kind could live`, `all siblings` intact. THRESHOLD: none. EXCEPTION: none carved out; the close condition `a point fix that leaves the siblings standing is a status, never a landing (SPEC INV-26)` survives. OUTPUT/SIDE EFFECT: matrix row + red-on-bug test still cover "the class beyond the single instance".

**2. The three-question node fitness test (step 3, 81w).** Old `can it be tested alone · does a real second place need it · can it and its neighbour be worked in parallel without queuing on shared files — three yes … a single no is a flag to answer (name the plan …, or fold the carve back), and two or more no make it premature` → three explicit questions plus the same three verdicts. THRESHOLD: **three / one / two-or-more all present and unchanged** — this is exactly where a split usually drops a count, and it did not. EXCEPTION: the "name the plan that turns it to a yes, or fold the carve back" carve-out survives verbatim in substance.

**3. Mid-work re-door and the independence re-scan (81w).** Old `Re-fire the door mid-work the moment the work is about to create a surface or state its door doesn't grant: STOP, reclassify, continue by the right door. When the re-door creates a surface or state that did not exist …` → `Stop, reclassify, and continue by the right door. The re-door sometimes creates a surface or state that did not exist when the lanes opened. In that case the same re-check **re-runs the independence edges against every rolling lane (SPEC INV-131)**.` CONDITION: `When …` → `sometimes … In that case` — same trigger, restated. SCOPE: `every rolling lane` unchanged. SIDE EFFECT: `pulls the re-doored lane back to serial … with a board line` → `The board carries a line for that move` — same artifact. The tail `The integration re-fence [INV-39] still catches the collision at landing; this closes the board's observability gap and adds no new net` is untouched.

**4. The push rule, step 9 (78w).** `PUSH accepted work there by rule (SPEC INV-82): every gate the diff reaches ran and passed …, plus the host's own push lines; the remote is discovered from the tree, and only a host with no remote gets one contextual question …` → `The push stands on two things. First, … Second, … The remote is discovered from the tree. Only a host with no remote gets one contextual question at the first push moment.` The restrictive **"only"** — the one word that carries the whole rule here — survives at the front of its own sentence. `one contextual question` count intact; the GitHub/GitLab/stay-local option set intact.

**5. The authoring seat (77w).** `the release pass may not waive it: a release's adversarial pass — the full re-prove at the release gate — is authored by a fresh seat, never the seat that authored the change` → `The freshness above is the whole rule, and the release pass may not waive it. A release's adversarial pass is the full re-prove at the release gate. It is authored by a fresh seat, never the seat that authored the change.` FORCE: `may not waive` and `never the seat that authored` both intact — no softening. The mechanical-floor clause keeps all three conditions (`exists`, `is release-dated`, `names a different seat`) and keeps `the rest is a discipline the seat holds`.

Now the style repairs.

**6. The admitted change (item 5 of my brief).** Old: `So the pipeline is not trusted, it is ENFORCED: a guardrails check the project wires to a git pre-push hook (+ the suite), so a change that fails ANY of these is RED and CANNOT be pushed.` New: `So the pipeline is enforced by a machine. The project wires a guardrails check to a git pre-push hook, beside the suite. A change that fails any of these reds, and cannot be pushed.` **Judgment: the negated half carried no requirement.** "not trusted" is not addressed to anyone and imposes no duty; it is rhetorical contrast. Everything operative is preserved and, if anything, sharpened: the actor moves from the vague passive to `The project wires`; `(+ the suite)` → `beside the suite` (the suite is still part of the net); `CANNOT be pushed` → `cannot be pushed` is case only. The one thing lost is the *emphasis* that a human's discipline is not the mechanism — but "enforced by a machine" states that positively, which is the lane's whole point.

**7. The honest boundary — an "X, not Y" frame where Y did carry an exclusion.** Old: `guardrails catch STRUCTURAL defects …. They do NOT catch a subtle SEMANTIC bug (is the number right?) — that still needs product-prover + a human's eyes.` New: `guardrails catch structural defects — …. A subtle semantic bug (is the number right?) stands outside their reach, and still needs product-prover + a human's eyes.` This is the exact case my brief warned about, and the exclusion **survives**: "stands outside their reach" is the same carve-out, and the fallback (`still needs product-prover + a human's eyes`) is intact. The five structural defect kinds are all still enumerated.

**8. The removal tombstone — the one place I'd call a real, small precision loss.** Old (`bp_old.md` L120): `spec section → dated REMOVED tombstone · matrix rows retired (not left "BUILT")`. New (`bp_new.md` L146-147): `The spec section becomes a dated tombstone marked removed. The matrix rows are retired, and none is left standing as built.` `BUILT` is a **status-vocabulary literal** — `docs/attic/2026-07-22-pre-format/TEST_MATRIX.md:40` defines `BUILT (test exists and runs green) · TODO · RETIRED`, and `tests/test_traceability.py:256` parses it. De-quoting and lowercasing it means a reader can read "built" as an ordinary adjective rather than the row's status value. ACTOR/FORCE/SCOPE/CONDITION are unchanged and the negation is preserved by `none is left`, so the instruction still instructs; nothing is pinned on it by any test; and `retired` was already lowercase in the old text, so the pattern is consistent. **Acceptable, but it is the weakest point in the diff** and the one I would fix first: restoring `` `BUILT` `` (backticked, which would also survive the caps-shout lint) costs nothing.

**9. Imperative → description, instance A.** Old: `never a stall on a knob you can reasonably pick (SPEC INV-70)` → `A knob you can reasonably pick never stalls the work (SPEC INV-70).` The prohibition moves from the reader to the knob. The `never` is retained and the invariant code anchors the duty, so the force is not softened to "should"; but the actor is now inanimate. Acceptable — the surrounding sentences (`No confirmation is requested; silence is consent, never re-asked`) keep the reader as the bound party.

**10. Imperative → description, instance B.** Old: `don't gate on resolving all of them` → `The step does not gate on resolving all of them.` Here the shift is benign in a way (9) is not: this sentence grants a permission rather than imposing a duty, so recasting it as a property of the step loses no obligation. The duty in the same passage — `Resolve every ⟨DECIDE⟩ that the surfaces under change touch` — stays imperative.

**11. Imperative → description, instance C.** Old: `Commit when green with no regression (unasked) — same or better is enough, never wait for perfect.` New: `Commit when green with no regression (unasked). Same or better is enough, and the work never waits for perfect.` Same pattern as (9). The governing imperative `Commit when green` is untouched, and `never` survives; only the anti-perfectionism clause became descriptive. Acceptable, and worth naming because three instances of the pattern is a habit, not an accident — if this lane runs again on another file, that habit is the thing to watch.

**12. The pack banner (top of file).** Old ran the fifteen shared rules as a parenthetical inside a 60-word sentence ending `live ONCE in the pack's base skill, live-spec-base (v5.0.0), together with the settings ladder`. New states the home first, then lists the rules. I counted the roster both sides: **fifteen members, same order, same wording**, `v5.0.0` intact, `Used standalone, this note is plain advice` intact. `ONCE` → `in one place` — same claim.

**13. The skip boundary.** Old: `**Skip the pipeline only if ALL hold:** single file · no new state / element / user-visible behaviour · an existing test level already covers the touched fact (still ship a test; …)`. New: `**Skip the pipeline only where all three of these hold.**` + three sentences + `A skip still ships a test.` THRESHOLD: the rewrite **invented a number** — "three" — where the old said "ALL". I checked: the old chain is exactly three conditions, so "three" is true and, being checkable, is stronger than "ALL". The parenthetical duties (`red first by default`, `a one-batch fix owes the mechanical red proof`), the `spec-backed-literal tripwire` with `(SPEC INV-104)`, and `Anything touching visibility / layout / colour enters at the matrix step minimum` all survive.

**14. The craft ladder (SPEC INV-33).** A `·`-chained roster of eight craft assignments became eight sentences of the form "The X is judged as … judges it". I counted both sides: **eight entries, same crafts, same qualifiers** — including `verify — the visitor's own fresh eyes, the builder's own view set aside` and `commit & show — a careful release hand whose reader is the human`. The following paragraph's `The craft takes the work-kind's form (SPEC INV-22, INV-33)` keeps both codes.

**15. Process bookkeeping (SPEC INV-61) — the "never scaled" list.** Old: `Never scaled: the law's own text, the red-first test, the delta's prove, the gates.` New: `Four things never scale: the law's own text, the red-first test, the delta's prove, and the gates.` Four members both sides; `never` retained; the `SHORT-FORM` record's three lines (`previous records clean · the delta in one line · the verdict`) survive verbatim, as does the small-delta definition.

## Every place meaning shifted at all, and why each is acceptable

- **`"BUILT"` → `built`** (passage 8) — a status literal lost its quotes and case. The instruction survives; nothing pins it; but this is the single thing I'd change. See above.
- **Three imperative→descriptive recasts** (`never wait for perfect`, `never a stall on a knob`, `don't gate on resolving`) — all keep `never`/`not` and their invariant codes; none downgrades must→should; two of the three govern permissions or attitudes rather than actions.
- **~60 ALL-CAPS words lowercased.** This is not incidental: the census's `style` count is `spec-style-lint`'s `caps-shout` rule, so these *are* the 110→33 style repairs. I checked each cap that could be a literal rather than emphasis: `BUILT` (above), `REMOVED` (no literal anywhere in templates/spec/tests), `RESOLVED` (no literal anywhere). The caps that carry meaning were deliberately **kept**: `FEATURE`, `INVARIANT`, `CLOSED`, `APPLIED`/`STOOD DOWN`, `FULL`/`CROSS-LINK`, `BOTH`/`NEVER`, `SHORT-FORM`, `HALTS`, `WRITING ITS OWN SAVED BYTES`, `MINOR`, `PUSH`.
- **`SEE/TRY ask` → `An ask that only wants to see or try something`** — a compressed compound became prose; the destination (`the labelled prototype home`, `base rule 16`) and the return condition (`only at promotion`) both survive.
- **`A full pass at an M-1 or M-6 gate that proves ARCHITECTURE.md beside the spec (INV-116) also appends…`** → `A full pass at an M-1 or M-6 gate proves ARCHITECTURE.md beside the spec (INV-116). Such a pass also appends…`. A restrictive relative clause became an assertion plus an anaphor. The referent set is identical because INV-116 makes the proving obligatory for exactly those gates, so no pass gains or loses the append duty.
